name: gap_fade_large_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, large overnight gaps (>0.3%) driven by SGX Nifty futures and US equity moves cause retail market-on-open orders to push the index further in the gap direction during the first 30-90 seconds of trading, extending price beyond the fair open implied by pre-market futures. Institutional market makers — who have already hedged their overnight gamma exposure — absorb this directional retail flow and gradually fade the intra-session extension back toward session VWAP. At 5-second resolution, we detect the stall of this extension: RSI(12) reaches short-term extremes in the gap direction while 30-second momentum turns against the extension, signaling the handoff from retail-driven momentum to institutional fading. We enter the first 15-90 second leg of the reversal, capturing the initial snap-back rather than the full 30-150 minute fade the original equity strategy targeted.

indicators.name: gap_pct
indicators.purpose: Scalar daily gap. No scaling — this is a session-level measure computed once per day from the first bar's open vs previous day's last close. The 0.3% threshold for NIFTY (vs 1.5% for individual stocks) is calibrated to index volatility: a 0.3% NIFTY gap is approximately 60+ spot points, which creates measurable intraday extension pressure.

indicators.name: extension_from_open
indicators.purpose: Measures how far price has moved intra-session from the day's open in the gap direction. On a gap-up day, positive extension means price is moving further from prev_close — this is what we fade. Replaces the original's 'excess_gap' (stock vs index) because on the index itself there is no reference instrument to compute excess against; the session extension from day_open serves the same role of detecting over-extension.

indicators.name: rsi_12
indicators.purpose: 12 bars = 60 seconds of RSI. The original used RSI(14) on 1-minute bars (14 minutes of data). We deliberately match the SAME TIME WINDOW (1 minute) rather than the same bar count, because the exhaustion threshold is time-based: retail over-extension at open typically peaks within 60 seconds. RSI > 70 on a gap-up day extension signals overbought exhaustion; RSI < 30 on gap-down extension signals oversold exhaustion.

indicators.name: mom_6
indicators.purpose: 6 bars = 30 seconds of momentum. Detects the turning of the intra-session extension: when momentum shifts against the gap direction (mom_6 turns negative on a gap-up extension day), institutional fading has begun. Replaces the original's MACD cross on 1-minute bars — MACD requires 35 bars warmup (29+9-min equivalent) which would span 2.5 minutes; at 5s bars we need a faster signal to catch the early fade.

indicators.name: vix_close
indicators.formula: India VIX close, joined asof to spot bars
indicators.purpose: Filter: VIX < 25 (same as original). When VIX > 25, large gaps are often driven by structural/fundamental events (e.g., budget, RBI policy), not behavioral overreaction — the gap does not fade.

conditions: extension_from_open < -ext_threshold (price extended further below open, e.g., -0.05%)
mom_6 > 0 (30s momentum turning upward: fade starting)
time_minutes in [555, 630) (09:15-10:30 IST morning window only)
buy_ce.confirmation: All conditions true simultaneously on same 5-second bar. Fade the gap-down extension: buy CE.

conditions: extension_from_open > ext_threshold (price extended further above open, e.g., +0.05%)
mom_6 < 0 (30s momentum turning downward: fade starting)
time_minutes in [555, 630) (09:15-10:30 IST morning window only)
buy_pe.confirmation: All conditions true simultaneously on same 5-second bar. Fade the gap-up extension: buy PE.

exit.stop_rationale: 4 option points = ~8 NIFTY spot points at delta 0.5. If the gap extension deepens by 8+ spot points after entry, institutional flow is joining (not fading) the gap — the behavioral thesis is wrong and we cut. NIFTY 30-second typical move is 2-5 option pts; 4 pts is a tight stop calibrated to the very short hold.
exit.target_rationale: 7 option points = ~14 NIFTY spot points. The initial fade leg from an over-extended gap typically covers 15-25 spot points in the first 60-90 seconds as institutional fading absorbs the retail flow. We target 7 pts (conservative 50% capture of the median first leg) for 1:1.75 R:R, appropriate for a contrarian fade with ~55% win rate.
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 10:30 IST (630 minutes) — gap fades beyond this window are no longer behavioral but structural

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; above 25 large gaps are structural events, not behavioral overreactions
filters.time_filter: 09:15-10:30 IST only; gap fade setups after 10:30 have lower win rate as price discovery completes
filters.volume_filter: none — index volume at 5s bars is noisy; session-level gap and RSI exhaustion are primary signals
filters.trend_filter: gap_pct must exceed gap_threshold in magnitude; small gaps (<0.3%) are intraday drift, not behavioral over-reaction events
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution at close prices, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — gap fade is behavioral (retail FOMO/fear at open) and structurally persistent, but as options markets mature and algo participation increases the initial over-extension may compress

adaptation_notes: Three key changes from original: (1) Universe collapsed from NIFTY 50 stocks to NIFTY index itself — the same behavioral thesis (overnight emotional over-reaction fades) applies to the index, with gap_threshold lowered from 1.5% to 0.3% to match index volatility. (2) Hold time compressed from 30-150 minutes to 15-90 seconds — we target the FIRST leg of the fade at 5s resolution, not the full recovery. This required replacing MACD (too slow at 5s) with 30-second momentum (mom_6). (3) 'excess_gap' (stock vs index) dropped — on the index itself, extension_from_open (how far price moved intra-session from the day's opening print) replaces it, detecting the same over-extension concept without requiring a reference instrument.
weaknesses: Gap fades on NIFTY index are less reliable than on individual stocks because index gaps are typically smaller (<0.5%) and driven by pre-market futures adjustment — the 'over-extension' window is shorter and noisier
Morning session only (09:15-10:30): very few signals per day (0-2 average); requires monitoring for large gap days which occur only 10-15% of trading sessions
Structural gap-and-go risk: budget announcements, RBI rate decisions, FII sell-off days can create gaps that never fade — VIX filter helps but does not eliminate this
